- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) or neutral, model often overpredicts downward moves; reduce forecast bias and add slight upward correction.
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; apply a 2–5% upward bias to peak forecasts.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing true price direction — especially after 3–5 day sentiment shifts — so adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true breakout.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp moves; apply dampening factor (e.g., 0.8–0.9 multiplier) to forecast if recent 5-day range is > 3σ from mean.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by > 2.5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply upward correction rule: +0.5% per day until convergence or sentiment confirms trend.
